newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court says OCT imports to EU in '90/'91 may incur duties.
newsitem.headline: Court says OCT imports to EU in '90/'91 may incur duties.

text.p: The European Court of Justice said on Tuesday that goods imported into the European Union from overseas countries and territories (OCTs) in 1990 and 1991, but originating elsewhere, may be subject to tax.
The court noted that free trade guarantees between the EU and OCTs does not extend to goods originating outside the OCTs, but which might be found in free circulation there.
According to Community law, the amount of duty on goods coming into the EU through OCTs depends on whether a direct import to the EU would be subject to a higher tariff.
Goods which entered into an OCT, and were then imported into the EU between 1990 and 1991, will be subject to the difference between the OCT tariff rate and a higher EU rate, the court said.

Part Four of the EEC Treaty, and more particularly articles 132(1), 133(1) and 134, must be interpreted as meaning that on 25 June 1991 customs duties could be levied on imports into the Community of goods originating in non-member countries which were in free circulation in a country forming part of the overseas countries and territories, to the extent to which, in accordance with article 101 of Council decision 91/482/EEVC of 25 July 1991 on the association of the overseas countries and territories with the European Economic Community, the duties paid in the overseas country or territory in question were lower than the duties applicable in the Community.
